text: Read the brief, the proof's rules, bookings/store examples, listing.mjs (308 lines) and parts of check.mjs (~150 lines) to learn what the tool reads; then the module's 3 source files (1310 lines) and call sites in users (grep, ~60 lines). Real state: check refuses 179 (39 in src, 138 in tests, 2 rules of form), 305 cannot-tell; listing 99 anything. Private #members of class AiUse are listed as entries (AiUse##x), contributing many 'anything'.

False start: stated each answer as an exact union (result | refusal kinds). The check then refused ~100 more places in the module's own tests: JS reads fields (r.code, r.limits, r.estimate) of the answer without narrowing, which TypeScript refuses on a union whose members lack the field. Also three of my comments disagreed with code (let change = null captured in a closure; whoseOf widening to string; use not narrowed by USE_KINDS.includes). Trying a OneOf<...> helper kind that gives each member the others' fields as optional undefined.

kindsUndetermined.why: handles of record-core, membership, ai-accounts and connections, none of which states a kind; I wrote * and named in words the members read

kindsUndetermined.why: the module's own tests pass numbers and booleans on purpose to show they are refused, never thrown; the code accepts any value, so * with a @bound

falseStarts: Stated each answer as a plain union of its result and refusal kinds: ~100 new refusals in the module's own tests, which read r.code / r.limits / r.estimate before telling which member they hold. Replaced with a OneOf<...> helper (each member carries the others' fields as optional undefined).
corrections: let change = null captured by a closure in aiLimitSet: typed * (TypeScript keeps it narrowed to null)
whoseOf widened to string: gave it a @type
use and mode not narrowed by USE_KINDS.includes / ASK_USAGE_MODES.includes: two casts in estimate, one in countAskUsage
#limitReached's start and whose not narrowed in the reached branch: cast period_start; LimitReachedRefusal.whose had to be Whose | null although never null there
Refusal.check and translation stated string, not string | null (every code has its row)
AiUseWordKey union first written with the type on its own line: the comment parser refused it; moved onto the @typedef line
notes: Real state: 179 refusals (39 src incl. 1 rule of form, 138 tests, 1 rule of form in a test fixture), 305 cannot-tell; listing 99 lines with anything. Commented: 149 refusals = 35 bound lines without a named test (expected, not fixed) + 10 pre-existing in src (#used/#limits options defaulting to null) + 1 rule of form (JSON.parse of the module's own stored 'what' column is taken for a message) + 1 rule of form in test fixture + 102 in tests, of which 82 pre-existing, 2 pre-existing reworded, 18 new that my (true) comments cause: 11 'Object is possibly null' (TS 2531, which the check does not treat as cannot-tell while it does 18047) where tests read useCheck(...).x knowing it is not null; 5 reads of a field of a OneOf union (string|undefined passed to a string-only assert); 1 estimate.unit read on an Estimate that may be the words 'not known yet'; 1 probe passing a usage without output_tokens on purpose. Listing after: 72 lines with anything (was 99): ~40 are private #members of AiUse the tool lists as entries, the rest the * named in kindsUndetermined. Comments: ~650 lines added to index.mjs (55 typedefs incl. 8 @storedrows row kinds and one @optable), ~50 to checks.mjs, 1 to schema.mjs.
